payload.claim: No witness exercises a task page with at least one attempt but zero findings, so nothing proves the `findings` table is still rendered (with its header) when there is nothing to show. Changing this block to `findings_rows = _finding_rows(store, task_id); if findings_rows: sections.append(_table(findings_rows, _FINDING_COLUMNS, table_id="findings"))` would silently drop the table for every task that has not reached REVIEW yet, and all 24 tests in tests/test_view_server.py still pass: every test that has attempts but no recorded findings (e.g. test_a_task_page_lists_each_attempt_once_with_its_times_turns_and_cost, test_a_task_page_heads_with_its_state_risk_batch_pull_request_and_cost's unbatched_task, test_a_task_page_shows_each_attempts_gate_outcomes_with_error_apart_from_fail) never looks at page.table_ids or page.tables['findings']. Criterion 5's claim that a task page with attempts always holds 'attempts, gate-results, its failures tables and findings in that order' is only witnessed for the case where every one of those tables happens to be non-empty; the test comment at tests/test_view_server.py:1573 ('So every table it reads has a row') shows this was a deliberate, acknowledged gap rather than an oversight, but it leaves the common no-findings (and no-gate-result) case unproven.
